papers.title: SpaReg: sparsity-based 3D reconstruction of tissue microenvironments at native resolution across morphological and spatial molecular modalities.
papers.abstract: Tissue microenvironments comprise cellular and acellular components whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture guides disease fate. Direct imaging of intact specimens by lightsheet and multiphoton microscopy, and computational reconstruction from serial sections, have established that 3D spatial context reveals cell and tissue organization inaccessible at single planes. Computational reconstruction in particular can leverage archived human tissue, benefiting from the cost-effectiveness, robustness, scalable storage, workflow compatibility, and century-long pathobiology knowledge of histology, a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SpaReg is a computational method that reconstructs 3D tissue microenvironments at native resolution from serial tissue sections, using a sparsity-based approach that works across both morphological (histology) and spatial molecular modalities. It enables 3D spatial context to be recovered from archived human tissue, avoiding the need for specialized 3D imaging and leveraging the cost-effectiveness and scalability of standard histology workflows.

papers.title: Genomic correlates of metastatic competence and progression in human melanoma.
papers.abstract: Genomic events and their timing that grant a primary tumour the competence to disseminate remain poorly defined. We performed sequencing of 247 stage I/II primary cutaneous melanomas (CMs) and 60 matched metastases without intervening therapy from a prospectively followed registry cohort with a median followup of 92 months, integrating copy-number, mutational, protein and spatial-transcriptomic analyses. Relapse was not distinguished by oncogenic point mutations, which were largely shared between primaries and metastases, but by somatic copy-number alterations (SCNAs) and global chromosomal in
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study sequenced 247 primary cutaneous melanomas and 60 matched metastases to identify genomic features that distinguish tumors that metastasize from those that do not. Relapse was not explained by oncogenic point mutations, which were largely shared between primaries and metastases, but rather by somatic copy-number alterations and global chromosomal instability. The findings suggest that chromosomal-level genomic changes, rather than specific driver mutations, confer metastatic competence in melanoma.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA Sequencing Analysis Reveals That Targeting PLG-PLGRKT Signaling-mediated Pro-fibrotic Scar-associated Macrophages Ameliorates Liver Fibrosis in Biliary Atresia.
papers.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a severe pediatric cholangiopathy characterized by rapidly progressive liver fibrosis. This study aimed to characterize scar-associated macrophages and investigate the role of plasminogen (PLG)-plasminogen receptor with a C-terminal lysine (PLGRKT) signaling in BA-associated fibrogenesis.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, this study identifies a population of pro-fibrotic scar-associated macrophages in the livers of children with biliary atresia, a pediatric bile duct disease that causes rapid liver fibrosis. The authors show that these macrophages are driven by PLG-PLGRKT signaling, and that blocking this pathway reduces liver fibrosis, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Macrophage-derived IL-27 sustains autoreactive CD8 + cytotoxic T cells in autoimmune hepatitis.
papers.abstract: Chronic or persistent T cell activation is widely thought to culminate in T cell exhaustion, yet how autoreactive CD8⁺ T cells remain functionally intact despite sustained self-antigen exposure is poorly understood. In chronic infection and cancer this durability is attributed to stem-like, TCF1⁺ PD-1⁺ progenitor-exhausted (Tpex) cells that reside in lymphoid tissue and continuously replenish functional effectors; whether such a reservoir operates within a chronically inflamed peripheral organ during sterile autoimmunity is unknown. Here we show that mice lacking the lysosomal nuclease DNase2a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study shows that in autoimmune hepatitis, macrophage-derived IL-27 sustains autoreactive CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, helping explain how these cells remain functional despite chronic self-antigen exposure rather than becoming exhausted. The authors identify a stem-like TCF1+ PD-1+ progenitor-exhausted (Tpex) reservoir operating within a chronically inflamed peripheral organ during sterile autoimmunity, using mice lacking the lysosomal nuclease DNase2a.

papers.title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in d
papers.summary: This study uses a highly multiplexed imaging dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to map mTOR signalling activity across different cell types in the tumour microenvironment. The analysis reveals distinct roles for mTOR signalling in different TME components, showing how multiplexed spatial profiling can disentangle complex pathway activity that varies by cell type.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for indexing protein databases, extending run-block compression to scale better with alphabet size. On RefSeq prokaryotic and viral proteins, it reduces memory footprint by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable running time, enabling efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: The authors present crumblr, a scalable statistical method for analyzing changes in cell type composition from single-cell data. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs and count ratio data, making it suitable for large cohort studies. The tool is designed to be fast and flexible for identifying shifts in cell type frequencies associated with health and disease.

papers.title: Variation in enhancer activity across brain regions defines neurological disease risk and shapes cellular pathology.
papers.abstract: Genetic variants associated with neurological traits are enriched in enhancers active in neurons. However, there are many types of neurons with varying functions across the brain, making it difficult to pinpoint insights into disease pathology. We set out to investigate whether cell type and brain region specificity of transcriptional enhancers could reveal new insights into the cellular pathology of neurological traits.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how enhancer activity differs across brain regions and neuron types, aiming to link genetic risk variants for neurological diseases to specific cellular contexts. The authors propose that region- and cell-type-specific enhancers can help pinpoint the cellular pathology underlying neurological traits.

papers.title: STAT3D as a new image-tailored Xenium-based spatial transcriptomics tool for accurately dissecting the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables researchers to study gene expression within tumor microenvironments at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue architecture. However, analyzing spatial omics data is challenging due to the complexity of the outputs, including large-scale images, millions of transcripts, and numerous spatial coordinates. Moreover, standard volumetric segmentation is often hampered by optical blurring and signal bleed-through in out-of-focus z-planes, which built-in tools in current platforms (e.g. Xenium Explorer) cannot solve. To overcome these challenges, we introduce ST
papers.summary: STAT3D is a new computational tool for analyzing Xenium spatial transcriptomics data that addresses limitations of existing platforms like Xenium Explorer, particularly problems with optical blurring and signal bleed-through in out-of-focus z-planes during volumetric segmentation. The tool is designed to more accurately dissect tumor microenvironments at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue architecture.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax introduces an annotation-independent archive that stores molecular evidence from single-cell RNA-seq experiments in a compact form, rather than relying on a gene-by-cell count matrix tied to a specific gene annotation. This allows the underlying evidence to be reinterpreted as annotations are revised, without needing to reprocess large raw reads or alignments. The approach addresses the problem that count matrices are frozen outputs of a computation whose annotation inputs change over time.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche linked to neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy non-response remains a major challenge in bladder cancer, yet the endothelial states and intercellular communication programs associated with treatment failure remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic data, computational analyses, and in vitro experiments to characterize endothelial programs associated with chemotherapy response. A non-response-related transcriptional program was preferentially enriched in endothelial cells and was most prominent in the TipEC_2 tip-like endothelial subset. Integrative an
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomics to identify endothelial cell states associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The authors find that a non-response transcriptional program is enriched in endothelial cells, particularly a tip-like subset (TipEC_2) marked by DLL4, suggesting this endothelial niche contributes to treatment failure. In vitro experiments support the computational findings.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies SERPINE1 as a vascular endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance remains a major obstacle in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet the contribution of the vascular microenvironment and its variation across HPV statuses remains unclear.
papers.summary: Using single-cell spatial transcriptomics, this study maps the vascular microenvironment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and identifies SERPINE1 in endothelial cells as a mediator of cisplatin resistance, with variation across HPV status. The finding highlights endothelial-derived signals as a therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance.

papers.title: Cell-resolved spatial mapping of antibody-drug conjugate targets in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) activity and target-dependent on-target/off-tumor toxicity depends in part on which cells express the target antigen, a feature that bulk assays cannot resolve.
papers.summary: This paper uses spatial mapping to identify which specific cell types within breast tumors express the targets of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), addressing a gap that bulk expression assays cannot fill. The approach reveals cell-level heterogeneity in ADC target expression, which is relevant to both efficacy and on-target/off-tumor toxicity. The work provides a framework for using spatial profiling to guide ADC target selection and safety assessment.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. They then profiled the gene expression of these cells, which are heavily parasitized and hemophagocytic, to characterize their biology in vivo. This provides the first transcriptomic signature of tissue MGCs in an infectious disease context, suggesting roles in parasite persistence and pathology.

papers.title: Spatial Atlas of Small Cell Lung Carcinoma Reveals Intratumoral Tumor-State Heterogeneity and an MMP12+ Macrophage Niche.
papers.abstract: Small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) is a highly aggressive tumor with a dismal prognosis among lung cancers. Treatment is failing because of primary or rapidly developing secondary resistance. Recent molecular studies have suggested four SCLC subtypes with unique therapeutic vulnerabilities-ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and YAP. These subtypes still distinguish themselves by considerable intra-tumoral heterogeneity and the influence of the microenvironmental context, which are both considered to be responsible for treatment resistance. We integrated in situ hybridization-based spatial transcriptomics w
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics to map small cell lung carcinoma tumors, revealing that the four known molecular subtypes (ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, YAP) coexist within individual tumors rather than being uniform per tumor. The authors also identified a distinct niche of MMP12+ macrophages associated with specific tumor states, highlighting how the tumor microenvironment contributes to heterogeneity and likely treatment resistance.

papers.title: A renal cyst-clear cell renal cell carcinoma comorbidity analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts.
papers.abstract: Renal cystic conditions are heterogeneous. We used a broad renal cyst-associated disease-gene framework to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression.
papers.summary: The authors analyzed genes associated with renal cystic diseases to find molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without assuming a direct cyst-to-cancer progression model. They identified a FOXM1-positive epithelial signaling axis involving COL6A1 and CD44 that remodels surrounding fibroblasts, suggesting a comorbidity-relevant tumor-stroma interaction.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics to build a compact risk score for predicting pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, identifying a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program associated with poor outcomes. The work links a specific gene signature to reduced immune activity and characterizes the cellular programs underlying metastatic risk.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics uncovers an invasive-desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and profound spatial heterogeneity, yet the multicellular organizational principles governing its tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; n = 9) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 4), integrating 61,234 single cells and 30,430 spots to identify an invasive-frontier myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast (IF-myCAF), which is characterized by elevated expression of ACTA2, TAGLN, COL11A1, THBS2, CTHRC1, and POSTN. IF-myCAFs were validated i
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular organization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, identifying a distinct myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast population (IF-myCAFs) enriched at the tumor invasive frontier. These IF-myCAFs, marked by genes such as ACTA2, COL11A1, and POSTN, form a spatially organized invasive-desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.abstract: Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood.
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics to malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) to map the spatial niches that drive intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion, and malignant transformation from benign precursor lesions. By profiling gene expression while preserving tissue architecture, the authors identify spatial trajectories associated with the transition from benign neurofibromas to aggressive MPNSTs, offering insight into how distinct microenvironments shape tumor progression in NF-1 and sporadic cases.

papers.title: Single-cell, spatial, and machine learning analyses identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-anchored palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline, yet most candidate therapies targeting amyloid-β have failed to robustly modify disease progression, underscoring an incomplete mechanistic understanding. Oligodendrocytes (ODCs) have recently emerged as active contributors to AD pathology, but the cell-type-specific role of protein S-palmitoylation - a reversible lipid post-translational modification regulating membrane targeting and trafficking - in AD remains uncharacterized. Here we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis combining single
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning to identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-specific, palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker for Alzheimer's disease. The work highlights oligodendrocytes as active contributors to AD pathology and links protein S-palmitoylation—a reversible lipid modification affecting membrane trafficking—to AD mechanisms in a cell-type-specific manner. ANKIB1 emerges as a potential biomarker warranting further validation.

papers.title: Histone H4K5 lactylation-driven feedback loop modulates glycerol-linked immunosuppressive activity of tumor-associated T regulatory cells.
papers.abstract: Tumor metastasis is the leading cause of death for more than 90% of cancer patients, with colorectal cancer (CRC) mainly spreading to the liver. The colon and liver possess distinct nutritional microenvironments, yet how these differences shape the tumor immune landscape remains unclear. Using single-cell analysis of autologous samples from CRC patients with liver metastases, we identified a distinct CD177+GK+ regulatory T (Treg) cell subset in metastatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that these GK+ Tregs localize at the tumor-adjacent interface and interact with immunosuppressive
papers.summary: Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of colorectal cancer liver metastases, the authors identified a distinct CD177+GK+ regulatory T cell subset enriched at the tumor-adjacent interface of metastatic lesions. They show that histone H4K5 lactylation drives a feedback loop that sustains glycerol-linked immunosuppressive activity in these Tregs, linking the nutrient microenvironment of the liver to immune evasion.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: NoiBic is a new biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise in high-throughput gene expression data, addressing the problem that technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and hinder functional module discovery. The method aims to recover meaningful biclusters that would otherwise be missed by noise-sensitive approaches.

papers.title: Mapping the Tissue Architecture and Endothelial-PEC Network in HAML Using Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) is a rare variant of perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasms (PEComas). Unlike its more common renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), the unique spatial microenvironment of HAML and its specific progression mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics from three sporadic HAML cases. We mapped functionally heterogeneous PEComas subpopulations and their localized tissue niches. Transcriptomic alignment and spatial colocalization demonstrated a high similarity between endothelial cells and a subset of PEC
papers.summary: This study combines single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics on three sporadic hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) cases to map the tissue architecture of this rare PEComa variant. The authors identify functionally heterogeneous PEComa subpopulations and their local niches, and show that endothelial cells closely resemble a subset of perivascular epithelioid cells in both transcriptome and spatial colocalization, suggesting an endothelial–PEC network. This provides the first spatially resolved characterization of the HAML microenvironment.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program. Unlike trajectory-based methods that assign genes to one module, it accommodates the many-to-many structure of regulation, where cells run multiple programs simultaneously and genes participate in several. This allows more faithful decomposition of single-cell expression into overlapping biological processes.

papers.title: Serval: a modular framework for decoding imaging based spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics technologies have opened new avenues for studying cellular organization and gene expression within intact tissues. However, the accuracy of downstream analyses depends critically on the decoding step that reconstructs barcodes from fluorescence patterns and maps them to gene identities. Despite a growing number of decoding methods, systematic benchmarking has been limited.
papers.summary: Serval is a modular framework for decoding barcodes in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, addressing the critical step of mapping fluorescence patterns to gene identities. It enables systematic benchmarking of decoding methods, which has been limited despite the growing number of available tools. The framework aims to improve the accuracy and comparability of downstream spatial analyses.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury models to characterize cell adhesion-related gene signatures. The authors identify CARG expression patterns across cell types and link them to inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption, nominating candidate therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to characterize the cellular landscape of ovarian cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The authors identify chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as key drivers of poor clinical outcomes, highlighting potential therapeutic targets in the residual fibroblast-enriched disease.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts biological age from bulk and single-cell RNA-seq as well as microarray data across diverse human tissues. Pasta's predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review argues that spatial transcriptomics, while valuable, captures only part of the picture, and that spatial epigenomic approaches are needed to understand how spatially restricted regulatory programs shape tumor behavior within intact tissue architecture. It surveys how spatial biology can be integrated into cancer epigenetics research, highlighting the gap left by bulk and single-cell methods that disrupt tissue context.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, allowing them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a unified timeline. They combined this with marker staining (Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp, S100b, Cd34, Dct/Tyrp2) and reanalysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to create a developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 computational pipelines (5 normalization methods × 4 clustering algorithms) across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, and find that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that seemingly technical preprocessing decisions can materially change downstream biological conclusions in cancer single-cell studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This study investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify the key microbial species involved and the molecular mechanisms by which they influence the disc microenvironment, though the abstract does not yet report specific findings.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration and machine learning identify an ACKR1+ endothelial cell-based lactate-immune signature associated with carotid plaque vulnerability and progression.
papers.abstract: Early identification of vulnerable carotid plaques is crucial for stroke prevention, but the upstream metabolic processes linked to endothelial transition and immune recruitment remain poorly defined. We characterised lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells (ECs) in human carotid plaques and derived a machine-learning signature for discriminating plaque vulnerability.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to characterize lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells within human carotid plaques. The authors derive a lactate-immune signature that can discriminate vulnerable from stable plaques, potentially aiding stroke risk stratification.

papers.title: Integrated scRNA-Seq and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal CHPF and GPC1 as Markers of Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Dominant Domains in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in the colorectal cancer (CRC) tumor microenvironment (TME) is closely related to stromal organization and may influence treatment-related features. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data from CRC tissues to examine cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains. GPC1 and CHPF were enriched in stromal regions and showed higher expression in CRC tissues than in normal tissues. In the analyzed cohorts, higher GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival ou
papers.summary: By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics of colorectal cancer tissues, the authors identified cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains within the tumor microenvironment. Two genes, GPC1 and CHPF, were enriched in these stromal regions, elevated in tumor versus normal tissue, and associated with advanced clinicopathological features and worse survival. These markers may help characterize stromal organization relevant to prognosis and treatment.

papers.title: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition and M2 macrophages drive aggressiveness in murine and human sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Patients with majority variant subtype histology including sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma (SUC) have poor outcomes and limited treatment options, and there are few preclinical resources to investigate rare histologic subtypes. We developed three novel variant subtype histology bladder cancer (BC) cell lines by finding that basal BC tumor cells derived from mice treated with N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl)-nitrosamine (BBN) were initially not competent to grow in immune competent mice, but then acquired tumorigenicity following passaging ("recycling") in mice lacking mature B and T cells. Three ge
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study establishes three new mouse-derived bladder cancer cell lines that model sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma, a rare and aggressive subtype with few research tools. By passaging basal tumor cells in immunodeficient mice, the authors generated tumorigenic lines and found that epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and M2 macrophage infiltration drive aggressiveness in both murine and human sarcomatoid tumors.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain.
papers.abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study
papers.summary: The authors present REBOSEP, a computational workflow for spatial transcriptomics data that detects tissue boundaries and measures gene expression as a function of distance from those boundaries. Applied to the developing mouse brain, it reveals that gene expression changes can be highly diverse and shift sharply across just a few cell layers at tissue boundaries. Hierarchical clustering of genes by their boundary-distance profiles uncovers shared regulatory patterns.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. The method aims to overcome common challenges such as limited sample sizes, variable cell counts, high dimensionality, and reliance on cell-type annotations. It offers a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study examines how the metabolic protein FDX1 relates to calreticulin (CALR) levels and JAK-STAT inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms. The authors report an association between FDX1 and CALR abundance along with inflammatory pathway activity, suggesting a link between metabolic programs and driver-genotype-related inflammation in MPNs.

papers.title: Integrative oxidative stress-disulfidptosis analysis identifies NPR3 and ZNF366 as cell-type-associated candidate markers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Disulfidptosis is a regulated cell-death program that occurs in SLC7A11-high cells under glucose limitation, but its relationship with oxidative stress in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains unclear. We integrated 313 oxidative stress-related genes with 24 disulfidptosis-related genes in the original TCGA-KIRC analysis. Pearson screening (|r| ≥ 0.8 and nominal two-sided P < 0.05) identified 21 disulfidptosis-oxidative stress (DOS) genes, from which three reported DOS subtypes, 63 subtype-associated genes and a four-gene score comprising ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3 and NPR3 were derived. In
papers.summary: This study integrates oxidative stress and disulfidptosis gene sets in TCGA clear cell renal cell carcinoma data to identify 21 overlapping genes and derive three molecular subtypes plus a four-gene prognostic score (ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3, NPR3). The authors propose NPR3 and ZNF366 as cell-type-associated candidate markers, though the work is largely correlative bioinformatics without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify candidate associations between the COX-2 pathway and the cholesteryl ester CE(20:4) along the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. Using computational analysis, the authors propose that this lipid feature may mark a CRC-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study integrates peripheral blood transcriptomic datasets to characterize gene expression programs distinguishing severe acute pancreatitis from mild disease. The authors identify NETosis-associated signatures and a pattern of adaptive immune suppression that stratifies severe cases, highlighting candidate mechanisms and potential biomarkers for early risk assessment.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for initial cluster generation with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to large datasets. It offers a practical tool for scalable single-cell clustering.

papers.title: Loss of CLIC3 in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes is associated with immune dysfunction and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether loss of the chloride channel protein CLIC3 in CD8+ cytotoxic T cells contributes to immune dysfunction in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors link reduced CLIC3 expression in these T cells to impaired immune function and worse patient prognosis, suggesting CLIC3 as a potential marker of T cell competence in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis identifies candidate hub genes and inferred regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory disorder of the skin. Despite the availability of targeted biologics like dupilumab, heterogeneous treatment responses persist, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers and a deeper understanding of cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis to identify candidate hub genes and infer regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis skin. The work aims to uncover cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment that may explain heterogeneous responses to biologics like dupilumab. It provides candidate biomarkers and regulatory insights for AD, though the abstract does not report specific validated findings.

papers.title: Genetic evidence and multi-omics characterization of DEHP-relevant detoxification and metabolic heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Human evidence linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited, and it remains unclear whether DEHP-relevant detoxification biology captures clinically meaningful HCC heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This study integrates genetic and multi-omics data to investigate whether DEHP (a common phthalate plasticizer) exposure and detoxification biology are linked to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) heterogeneity. It characterizes DEHP-relevant detoxification pathways and metabolic variation across HCC tumors, aiming to identify clinically meaningful subtypes. The work provides preliminary human evidence connecting phthalate exposure biology to HCC and suggests that detoxification-related metabolic heterogeneity may have clinical relevance.

papers.title: Cellular, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial contextualization of bulk transcriptional patterns linked to positive peritoneal cytology in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) identifies a clinically adverse subset of endometrial cancer, but the tumor transcriptional patterns accompanying PPC and their cellular origins remain incompletely resolved. We evaluated PPC-linked bulk RNA patterns in TCGA-UCEC and contextualized the resulting programs using independent single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial datasets.
papers.summary: This study links bulk transcriptional patterns associated with positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) in endometrial cancer to specific cell types and spatial contexts using single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial datasets. It identifies PPC-associated gene programs and traces their cellular origins, providing a more resolved view of the adverse biology underlying PPC.

papers.title: Mitochondrial metabolic plasticity in cancer: hybrid bioenergetic states and translational targeting in surgical oncology.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial metabolism is increasingly recognized as an active determinant of tumor growth and cancer-cell adaptation rather than solely a source of cellular energy. Mitochondrial metabolism supports tumor anabolism, while mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) alterations can affect respiratory chain function, redox homeostasis, and adaptation to changing tumor environments. At the same time, tumor metabolism is heterogeneous and flexible and cannot be explained by a uniform Warburg model. Tumor cells may use glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), or hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS states, with the re
papers.summary: This review argues that mitochondrial metabolism actively shapes tumor growth and adaptation rather than merely supplying energy, and that mtDNA alterations influence respiratory chain function, redox balance, and environmental adaptation. It emphasizes that tumor metabolism is heterogeneous and flexible, with cells adopting glycolytic, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), or hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS states that the classic Warburg model cannot capture. The authors discuss translational implications for targeting these bioenergetic states in surgical oncology.

papers.title: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and vasculogenic mimicry in tumor vascular plasticity: a comparative bibliometric analysis and mechanistic framework.
papers.abstract: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM) are distinct forms of cellular and vascular plasticity that may contribute to tumor vascular adaptation. Although they have largely evolved as separate research fields, emerging experimental observations suggest potential convergence in their regulation by the tumor microenvironment.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis compares the research landscapes of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM), two distinct mechanisms of tumor vascular plasticity. The authors propose a mechanistic framework suggesting these previously separate fields may converge through shared regulation by the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Targeting TREM2+ and TIMD4+ Macrophages Reprograms the Tumor Microenvironment and Enhances PD-1 Blockade Efficacy in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is the second most common primary liver cancer. Macrophages are crucial components of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2-positive (TREM2+) macrophages have recently emerged as potent pro-tumor progress players in several cancers. However, the heterogeneity and tumor-promoting mechanisms of macrophages especially TREM2+ macrophages in ICC remain systematically unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically elucidate the heterogeneity of macrophages in ICC, with a specific focus on the pr
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes macrophage heterogeneity in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, identifying TREM2+ and TIMD4+ macrophage populations as key pro-tumor players in the tumor microenvironment. Targeting these macrophage subsets reprograms the immunosuppressive microenvironment and improves the efficacy of PD-1 checkpoint blockade, suggesting a combination therapeutic strategy for this liver cancer.

papers.title: Applications of single-cell transcriptomics in glaucoma research: from the aqueous humor outflow pathway to retinal ganglion cell neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, driven by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration. While genetic and environmental risk factors have been identified, the cell-type-specific mechanisms underlying pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution analysis of cellular heterogeneity, developmental trajectories and intercellular communication networks. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq advances across two critical domains in glaucoma research: (1) aqueous humor outflow pathway (AHOP) phy
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent single-cell RNA sequencing studies in glaucoma research, focusing on two areas: the aqueous humor outflow pathway and retinal ganglion cell degeneration. It highlights how scRNA-seq reveals cell-type-specific mechanisms, cellular heterogeneity, developmental trajectories, and intercellular communication networks that were previously inaccessible with bulk approaches.

papers.title: Altered resting-state brain function in diabetic retinopathy: a meta-analysis of combined transcriptome-neuroimaging study.
papers.abstract: Patients with diabetes may develop cognitive dysfunction, particularly at advanced stages of the disease, manifested by impairments in learning, memory, language, and judgment. Previous studies have reported abnormal brain functional alterations in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR), which may be associated with cognitive impairment in diabetes; however, the molecular correlates of these brain alterations remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis combines resting-state neuroimaging findings with transcriptome data to identify brain functional alterations in diabetic retinopathy patients and link them to underlying molecular correlates. The study aims to connect abnormal brain activity patterns to gene expression profiles, potentially explaining cognitive impairment in diabetes.
